```{r setup}
slide_gt <- function(x, size = 18) {
  size <- round(size * 1.15)   # all tables 15% larger than their nominal size
  if (inherits(x, "gtsummary")) x <- gtsummary::as_gt(x)
  x |>
    gt::tab_options(
      table.font.size = gt::px(size), data_row.padding = gt::px(1),
      heading.title.font.size = gt::px(size + 2), footnotes.font.size = gt::px(size - 4),
      column_labels.font.weight = "bold", table.width = gt::pct(100)
    ) |>
    gt::sub_missing(missing_text = "")
}
# data frame -> slide table (variable labels dropped so column names show)

  df[] <- lapply(df, function(x) { attr(x, "label") <- NULL; x })
  slide_gt(gt::gt(df), size)
}
```

## Today

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
**One trial, end to end, the way a trial statistician works it.**

* Plan it: protocol, estimand, SAP, group sequential design, sample size
* Collect it: CRF, raw data, SDTM, ADaM
* Report it: TFL shells, tables and figures, the R packages behind them
* Monitor it: interim analysis, p-values, conditional power
* Submit it: datasets, metadata, reviewer's guides

Every number on these slides is computed live from the code in **`lab/`**,
which you can run on Posit Cloud or with Claude.
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
| Part | Topic | Min |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The map of a trial | 5 |
| 2 | Planning | 25 |
| 3 | Data standards | 20 |
| 4 | Tables, figures, listings | 20 |
| 5 | Interim analysis | 12 |
| 6 | Submission and wrap-up | 8 |
:::
::::

::: notes
Set expectations: this is not a methods lecture; it is how the methods you
learned are used when a real trial is run. Point students to the repository now
so they can follow along.
:::

## Acronyms: we will spell them out

Clinical trials run on acronyms. Each one is spelled out the first time it
appears, and the full list is in `lab/docs/00_glossary.md`.

:::: {.columns .small}
::: {.column width="50%"}
* **SAP**: Statistical Analysis Plan
* **CRF**: Case Report Form; **EDC**: Electronic Data Capture
* **CDISC**: Clinical Data Interchange Standards Consortium
* **SDTM**: Study Data Tabulation Model (collected data)
* **ADaM**: Analysis Data Model (analysis-ready data)
* **TFL**: Tables, Figures and Listings
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
* **PFS**: Progression-Free Survival; **OS**: Overall Survival
* **ORR**: Objective Response Rate
* **TEAE**: Treatment-Emergent Adverse Event
* **DMC**: Data Monitoring Committee
* **IA**: Interim Analysis; **DCO**: Data Cut-Off
* **CP**: Conditional Power
:::
::::

# Part 1 · The map of a trial {background-color="#1D4F91" .part-title}

5 minutes

## Where the statistician sits

```{=html}
<div class="flow">
  <div class="box lead"><b>Protocol</b>objectives, endpoints, sample size</div><div class="arrow">&rarr;</div>
  <div class="box lead"><b>SAP + shells</b>every analysis pre-specified</div><div class="arrow">&rarr;</div>
  <div class="box review"><b>CRF / EDC</b>collect what the SAP needs</div><div class="arrow">&rarr;</div>
  <div class="box review"><b>Raw data</b>EDC export + vendor files</div><div class="arrow">&rarr;</div>
  <div class="box review"><b>SDTM</b>standard tabulation</div>
</div>
<div class="flow">
  <div class="box review"><b>ADaM</b>analysis-ready datasets (statistician writes the specs)</div><div class="arrow">&rarr;</div>
  <div class="box review"><b>TFLs</b>tables, figures, listings</div><div class="arrow">&rarr;</div>
  <div class="box lead"><b>Clinical study report</b>interpretation</div><div class="arrow">&rarr;</div>
  <div class="box review"><b>Submission</b>eCTD module 5</div>
</div>
<div class="flow">
  <div class="box dashed"><b>Interim analysis</b>same ADaM + TFL programs on a data cut &rarr; Data Monitoring Committee &rarr; continue / stop</div>
</div>
```

[<span class="legend-lead"></span> statistician leads &nbsp;&nbsp; <span class="legend-review"></span> statistician specifies and reviews]{.small}

:::: {.columns .small}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Statistician owns**: design, sample size, SAP, shells, ADaM specifications,
interim plan, interpretation.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Works with**: clinicians (endpoints), data management (CRF, cleaning),
statistical programmers (SDTM, ADaM, TFL code), regulatory (submission).
:::
::::

::: notes
The arrow back from the interim analysis is the reason group sequential
designs exist. Programmers write most of the code, but the statistician signs
off on what the code must do.
:::

## Our running example: CDISCPILOT01

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
* Data from **pharmaverse** (`pharmaversesdtm`, `pharmaverseadam`):
  the CDISC SDTM/ADaM pilot study, xanomeline patch vs placebo
* Real CDISC structure: `r nrow(adsl)` patients screened,
  `r sum(adsl$ITTFL == "Y")` randomized 1:1:1
* plus **synthetic RECIST 1.1 tumour assessments** (`rs_onco`)
* For this course we treat it as an oncology trial:
  * **Primary**: PFS, High Dose vs Placebo
  * **Secondary**: PFS Low Dose vs Placebo, ORR, OS
  * **Safety**: adverse events, laboratory tests
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r}
adsl |>
  dplyr::mutate(Arm = factor(TRT01P, levels = c(ARM_LEVELS, "Screen Failure"))) |>
  dplyr::count(Arm, name = "Patients") |>
  tab(20)
```
:::
::::

::: {.takeaway}
Design numbers are for teaching; the data are reported as they are.
:::

# Part 2 · Planning {background-color="#1D4F91" .part-title}

Protocol, estimand, SAP, group sequential design, sample size (25 minutes)

::: notes
Target: finish Part 2 by minute 30. Emphasise that every later step implements a decision made here.
:::

## Protocol: the statistician's sections

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
| | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| Primary | **PFS**: randomization to first progression (RECIST 1.1, investigator) or death |
| Key secondary | PFS, Low Dose vs Placebo |
| Secondary | **ORR**: best overall response CR or PR |
| Secondary | **OS**: randomization to death |
| Safety | TEAEs (MedDRA), labs (CTCAE grades) |

[RECIST: Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors; CR/PR: complete/partial response; MedDRA: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities; CTCAE: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events]{.tiny .muted}
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Also written by the statistician**

* Hypotheses and alpha: H0: HR = 1 vs H1: HR < 1, one-sided 2.5%
* Design: 1:1:1, event-driven, one interim analysis
* Sample size and its assumptions
* Analysis populations and methods (summary)
* Multiplicity strategy
* Interim analysis and DMC charter

Full text: `lab/docs/01_protocol_synopsis.md`
:::
::::

## The estimand (ICH E9(R1))

An estimand says **what** we estimate *before* we decide **how**. ICH: International Council for Harmonisation.

| Attribute | PFS, High Dose vs Placebo |
|---|---|
| Population | All randomized patients (intention-to-treat, ITT) |
| Treatment | High Dose vs placebo, on top of best supportive care |
| Variable | Time to progression (RECIST 1.1) or death |
| Intercurrent events | Stops treatment early: *treatment policy* (keep scanning) · Death: part of the endpoint (*composite*) · New anticancer therapy: *hypothetical* (censor before it) |
| Summary measure | Hazard ratio (Cox model), tested by log-rank |

::: {.takeaway}
Censoring rules are not programming details: they are how the estimand handles
intercurrent events. Write them in the SAP, then code them exactly.
:::

## SAP: decide everything before unblinding

:::: {.columns .small}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Definitions**

* Analysis sets and the ADSL flag for each
* Study day, baseline, visit windows
* Treatment-emergent AE window
* Partial date imputation (ADaM only, never SDTM)
* Endpoint derivations and **censoring rules**

**Methods**

* Test, model, stratification factors
* CI methods (exact? log-log?), handling of ties
* Sensitivity and subgroup analyses
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Error control**

* Multiplicity strategy across endpoints and doses
* Interim analyses: timing, boundaries, futility

**Outputs**

* TFL shells: every table, figure and listing, with titles, populations and footnotes

**Process**

* Final before database lock (DBL) and before anyone sees unblinded data

Excerpt: `lab/docs/02_sap.md`
:::
::::

## Analysis sets become ADSL flags

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
| Set | Definition | Flag |
|---|---|---|
| ITT | All randomized, **as randomized** | `ITTFL`, `TRT01P` |
| Safety | All dosed, **as treated** | `SAFFL`, `TRT01A` |

[ADSL: subject-level analysis dataset, one row per patient]{.small .muted}
:::
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
adsl |>
  dplyr::filter(ITTFL == "Y") |>
  dplyr::count(`Randomized (TRT01P)` = TRT01P, `Received (TRT01A)` = TRT01A, name = "Patients") |>
  tab(20)
```
:::
::::

::: {.takeaway}
`r sum(adsl$TRT01P == "Xanomeline High Dose" & adsl$TRT01A == "Xanomeline Low Dose")`
patients randomized to High Dose stopped during the 54 mg start and never got
81 mg: High Dose for efficacy, Low Dose for safety.
:::

## PFS censoring rules (SAP section 6.1)

| Situation | Date | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Progression documented (RECIST 1.1) | Date of the first scan showing progression | **Event** |
| Death before progression | Date of death | **Event** |
| No progression, no death | Last adequate tumour assessment | Censored |
| No post-baseline assessment, no death | Randomization | Censored |
| New anticancer therapy before progression | Last adequate assessment before it | Censored |
| Event after two or more missed scans | Last adequate assessment before the gap | Censored (sensitivity) |

[Adapted from FDA guidance *Clinical Trial Endpoints for the Approval of Cancer Drugs and Biologics* (2018). We will turn this table into code in Part 3.]{.small .muted}

## Why a group sequential design?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
* Look at the data **before** the planned end: stop early for efficacy, or for futility
* Each look is a chance for a false positive: spread the one-sided 2.5% over looks
* **Alpha spending function** (Lan-DeMets, O'Brien-Fleming type), with information fraction $t$ = events observed / events planned:

$$
\alpha(t) = 2\left[1 - \Phi\!\left(\frac{z_{1-\alpha/2}}{\sqrt{t}}\right)\right]
$$

* Spends almost nothing early and keeps the final boundary close to 1.96
:::
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 8.5
#| fig-height: 5.2
p_boundary
```
:::
::::

## The design in {rpact}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r design-gsd, opts.label = "code"}
```
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
```{r}
boundary_tbl |>
  dplyr::select(-`Months from first randomization`, -`Futility boundary (Z)`) |>
  tab(16)
```

* Interim efficacy needs p < `r signif(design$stageLevels[1], 2)`: about a 50% better hazard
* The final test is barely penalised: `r round(design$criticalValues[2], 3)` vs 1.960
* Futility is **non-binding**: ignoring it does not inflate alpha
:::
::::

## Sample size for survival: power comes from events

Schoenfeld's formula (1:1 allocation, log-rank test):

$$
d = \frac{4\,(z_{1-\alpha} + z_{1-\beta})^2}{(\log \mathrm{HR})^2}
= \frac{4\,(1.960 + 0.842)^2}{(\log 0.6)^2} \approx `r round(events_fixed, 1)`
$$

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r design-schoenfeld, opts.label = "code"}
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
* Fixed design: `r round(events_fixed, 1)` events
* × inflation factor `r round(inflation, 4)` for the interim
* = `r round(events_gsd, 1)` → **`r target_events` events**; interim at **`r ia_events`**

::: {.takeaway}
The number of patients only decides **how long** it takes to observe the events.
:::
:::
::::

## From events to patients

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
```{r design-samplesize, opts.label = "code"}
```
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
Assumptions: placebo median PFS `r DESIGN$median_control` months (placebo arms of
refractory colorectal cancer trials such as CORRECT and RECOURSE), HR 0.60, 24-month
accrual, 3-month minimum follow-up, 25% dropout by month 3.

* **`r round(ss$maxNumberOfSubjects, 1)` → `r 2 * n_per_arm` patients** (`r n_per_arm` per arm) for the primary comparison
* With the Low Dose arm: **`r 3 * n_per_arm`** planned; the study randomized `r sum(adsl$ITTFL == "Y")`
* Expected timing: interim at month `r round(ss$analysisTime[1, 1], 1)`, final at month `r round(ss$analysisTime[2, 1], 1)`
:::
::::

## How fragile is the plan?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r}
sens_tbl |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::tab_style(gt::cell_fill(color = "#EEF5FB"), gt::cells_body(rows = `Assumed HR` == 0.6)) |>
  slide_gt(20)
```
:::
::: {.column width="55%"}
* Events needed grow like $1 / (\log \mathrm{HR})^2$: HR 0.70 needs twice the events of HR 0.60
* The HR is the most important and least certain assumption: justify it from earlier trials
* Proportional hazards is an assumption too; delayed effects (common with immunotherapy) cost power
* Event-driven trials: monitor **pooled, blinded** event counts and re-forecast the analysis dates
:::
::::

# Part 3 · Data standards {background-color="#1D4F91" .part-title}

CRF → raw data → SDTM → ADaM (20 minutes)

::: notes
Target: finish Part 3 by minute 50. Students rarely see raw data; show the formats and the QC story.
:::

## Collect what the SAP needs, nothing else

| SAP needs | Comes from | Raw file in `lab/data/raw/` | SDTM |
|---|---|---|---|
| Randomized arm and date | IRT vendor transfer | `irt.csv` | DM.ARM, DS |
| Age, sex, race | Demographics CRF | `dm.csv` | DM |
| First / last dose, dose received | Exposure CRF | `ex.csv` | EX, DM |
| Progression | Tumour response CRF | `rs.csv` | RS |
| Death, end of study | End of Study CRF | `ds.csv` | DS |
| Adverse events | AE CRF + MedDRA coding | `ae.csv` | AE |
| Concomitant medications | CM CRF + WHODrug coding | `cm.csv` | CM |
| Laboratory values | Central lab transfer | `lb.csv.gz` | LB |

[IRT: Interactive Response Technology (randomization system); CM: concomitant medications; WHODrug: World Health Organization Drug Dictionary]{.small .muted}

## The annotated CRF: Adverse Event page

| CRF question | CRF field (CDASH) | Raw value | SDTM variable |
|---|---|---|---|
| Adverse event term | `AETERM` | APPLICATION SITE ERYTHEMA | `AETERM` |
| Start date | `AESTDAT` | 03 JAN 2014 · UN JAN 2014 | `AESTDTC` = "2014-01-03" · "2014-01" |
| Severity | `AESEV` | Mild / Moderate / Severe | `AESEV` = MILD / MODERATE / SEVERE |
| Serious? | `AESER` | Yes / No | `AESER` = Y / N |
| Relationship to study drug | `AEREL` | None / Remote / Possible / Probable | `AEREL` |
| (coding team) | `AETERM_PT`, `AETERM_SOC` | APPLICATION SITE ERYTHEMA | `AEDECOD`, `AEBODSYS` |
| (derived) | | | `AESEQ`, `AESTDY` |

[CDASH: Clinical Data Acquisition Standards Harmonization: CRF field names designed to map to SDTM. PT: preferred term; SOC: system organ class.]{.small .muted}

## Raw data look like this

```{r}
raw_ae <- read_raw("ae")
raw_ae |>
  dplyr::filter(SUBJECT %in% c("701-1015", "701-1023")) |>
  dplyr::select(SUBJECT, AETERM, AESTDAT, AEENDAT, AEONGO, AESEV, AESER, AEREL, AETERM_PT) |>
  head(7) |>
  tab(16)
```

:::: {.columns .small}
::: {.column width="33%"}
**EDC**: `"03 JAN 2014"`, unknown day `"UN JAN 2014"`, text pick-lists
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
**IRT vendor**: date "`r irt_date_example`"
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
**Lab vendor**: date "`r lb_example$COLL_DATE`", time "`r lb_example$COLL_TIME`", units in two systems
:::
::::

## Where did these raw data come from?

pharmaverse ships SDTM only, so the lab **reverse-engineers** raw data by undoing
what the SDTMIG (SDTM Implementation Guide) asks a sponsor to derive:

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
1. Drop derived variables: `--SEQ`, `--DY`, `USUBJID`, `AGE`, reference dates
2. ISO 8601 dates → CRF text
3. Controlled terminology → CRF display text
4. Keep dictionary codes as "coding" columns
5. Reshape findings the way forms and vendors deliver them
:::
::: {.column width="58%"}
```{r raw-date-helpers, opts.label = "code"}
```
:::
::::

## SDTM in one slide

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**One dataset per domain**, grouped in classes

* Special purpose: **DM** (demographics)
* Interventions: **EX** (exposure), **CM** (medications)
* Events: **AE** (adverse events), **DS** (disposition)
* Findings: **LB** (labs), **VS** (vitals), **RS** / **TU** / **TR** (tumour response, identification, results)
* Trial design: TA, TV, TS ...
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Conventions you will meet every day**

* `USUBJID`: unique across all studies of the sponsor
* Dates in ISO 8601 (`--DTC`), partial dates stay partial
* Study day `--DY`: **no day 0**
* `--SEQ`: unique record number within patient
* Controlled terminology (CT): `SEX` is `"F"` or `"M"`
* Non-standard variables go to SUPPQUAL (supplemental qualifiers), e.g. `SUPPDM`
:::
::::

## QC: compare with an independent version

```{r}
qc_summary |>
  tab(22)
```

:::: {.columns .small}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**DM `RFENDTC`, patient 01-710-1083.** The reference uses the date the end-of-study
page was completed; our rule uses the date of the event (death). A **spec ambiguity**:
fix the specification, not just the code.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**AE `AESTDY`, patient 01-716-1063.** The AE starts on the first-dose date, so the
study day is 1; the reference says 366. An **error in the reference data**.
:::
::::

::: {.takeaway}
Independent double programming (two programmers, one spec, compare with
{diffdf} or SAS PROC COMPARE) is how regulated outputs are checked.
:::

## ADaM: analysis-ready, traceable

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Principles (ADaMIG)**

* Analysis-ready: one procedure call away from the result
* Traceable: every value leads back to SDTM
* Documented by metadata (define.xml)

**Structures**

* **ADSL**: one row per patient
* **BDS** (Basic Data Structure): one row per patient × parameter × time point. ADLB, ADRS, **ADTTE**
* **OCCDS** (Occurrence Data Structure): ADAE, ADCM
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
| SDTM sources | ADaM dataset | Structure |
|---|---|---|
| DM, DS, VS, SUPPDM | **ADSL** | one row per patient |
| RS + ADSL | **ADRS** | BDS (response by visit, BOR, PD) |
| ADSL + ADRS | **ADTTE** | BDS (PFS, OS) |
| AE + ADSL | **ADAE** | OCCDS |
| CM + ADSL | **ADCM** | OCCDS |
| LB + ADSL | **ADLB** | BDS (with CTCAE grades) |

[Built with {admiral} (pharmaverse): one function per derivation rule.]{.small .muted}
:::
::::

## ADSL: add what our SAP needs {.code-small}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="62%"}
```{r adsl-derive, opts.label = "code"}
```
:::
::: {.column width="38%"}
```{r}
adsl_check |>
  dplyr::mutate(TRT01P = stringr::str_replace(TRT01P, "Xanomeline ", "")) |>
  tab(16)
```
:::
::::

## ADTTE: one row per patient per parameter

```{r}
adtte |>
  dplyr::filter(USUBJID %in% c("01-701-1015", "01-701-1023", "01-701-1028")) |>
  dplyr::select(USUBJID, PARAMCD, STARTDT, ADT, AVAL, CNSR, EVNTDESC, SRCDOM, SRCVAR, SRCSEQ) |>
  tab(18)
```

* `AVAL` = `ADT` − `STARTDT` + 1 (days); `CNSR` = 0 event, 1 censored
* `SRCDOM` / `SRCVAR` / `SRCSEQ`: **traceability** to the record that decided the date

# Part 4 · Tables, figures, listings {background-color="#1D4F91" .part-title}

Shells, computing, baseline, efficacy, safety (20 minutes)

::: notes
Target: finish Part 4 by minute 70. Use the Output/Code tabs; do not read every number.
:::

## TFL shells come with the SAP

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
**Table 14.2.1** Progression-free survival (ITT set)

| | Placebo (N=xx) | Low (N=xx) | High (N=xx) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Events, n (%) | xx (xx.x) | xx (xx.x) | xx (xx.x) |
| Censored, n (%) | xx (xx.x) | xx (xx.x) | xx (xx.x) |
| Median, months (95% CI) [a] | x.x (x.x, x.x) | ... | ... |
| HR vs placebo (95% CI) [b] | Reference | x.xx (...) | x.xx (...) |
| One-sided p (log-rank) | | x.xxx | x.xxx |

[[a] Kaplan-Meier, Brookmeyer-Crowley CI (log-log). [b] Cox model.]{.tiny}
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
* Written **before** data exist; agreed by statistician, clinician, programmers
* Fix: numbering (ICH E3: 14.1 baseline, 14.2 efficacy, 14.3 safety), titles, population, rows, statistics, decimals, footnotes
* Programmers code to the shell; QC checks against the shell
* All shells: `lab/docs/04_tfl_shells.md`
:::
::::

## The computing stack

| Step | R packages used here | Alternatives you will meet |
|---|---|---|
| Design, sample size | **rpact** | gsDesign, East (commercial), SAS PROC SEQDESIGN |
| Raw → SDTM | dplyr (by hand) | **sdtm.oak** (pharmaverse), SAS |
| SDTM → ADaM | **admiral**, admiralonco, metatools | SAS macros |
| Survival analysis | **survival**, ggsurvfit | SAS PROC LIFETEST / PHREG |
| Tables | **gtsummary** (+ cards), gt | rtables + tern, Tplyr, r2rtf |
| Interim data cut | admiral functions with a cut-off date | **datacutr** (pharmaverse) |
| Submission files | **xportr** | metacore, SAS |
| QC | **diffdf** | SAS PROC COMPARE |
| Reproducibility | **renv**, git | containers |

[pharmaverse (pharmaverse.org): open-source R packages for clinical reporting, built by pharmaceutical companies together.]{.small .muted}


## Why the curves look like stairs

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
* Progression is only **seen at scheduled scans** (weeks 6, 12, 18, 24)
* The true progression time is somewhere between two scans: **interval-censored**
* Many tied event times at each scan
* If one arm is scanned later or less often, PFS is biased: same schedule in every arm
* Sensitivity analysis: interval-censored methods (e.g. `icenReg`), or a midpoint imputation
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
pfs |>
  dplyr::filter(CNSR == 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Week = round(AVAL / 7)) |>
  dplyr::count(`Study week of progression` = cut(Week, c(0, 4, 8, 10, 14, 20, 30),
                                                labels = c("0-4", "5-8", "9-10", "11-14", "15-20", "21-30"))) |>
  tab(20)
```
:::
::::

## The log-rank test, by hand

$$
Z = \frac{\sum_j \left(O_{1j} - E_{1j}\right)}{\sqrt{\sum_j V_{1j}}},\qquad
E_{1j} = d_j \frac{n_{1j}}{n_j},\qquad
V_{1j} = d_j \frac{n_{1j}\, n_{0j}\,(n_j - d_j)}{n_j^2\,(n_j - 1)}
$$

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
logrank_parts |>
  tab(20)
```
:::
::::

Variance $V$ = `r round(logrank_var, 2)`, so
$Z = (E - O)/\sqrt{V}$ for High Dose = `r sprintf("%.1f", lr$exp[2] - lr$obs[2])` / `r sprintf("%.2f", sqrt(logrank_var))`
= **`r sprintf("%.3f", pfs_hi$z)`**, one-sided p = **`r fmt_p(pfs_hi$p_one_sided)`**.


Ties and CI methods change the numbers. The SAP must name the method
(e.g. "Efron ties; Brookmeyer-Crowley CI with log-log transformation"), and
double programming in R and SAS will not match unless both follow it.

## What can we claim? Multiplicity

```{r}
hier_tbl |>
  tab(20)
```

* The final boundary is recomputed with the **actual** information:
  `r ia_events_obs` events at the interim, `r pfs_hi$events` at the final → Z ≥ `r sprintf("%.3f", z_final)`
* Primary hypothesis not rejected (HR `r sprintf("%.2f", pfs_hi$hr)`): the chain stops, everything after it is **descriptive**
* Nominal p-values for later endpoints may be shown, but they support no claim

## TFL production in practice

:::: {.columns .small}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Before data**

* Shells signed off with the SAP
* ADaM specifications (one row per variable, with derivation)
* Programs written and run on **blinded** or dummy-treatment data ("dry runs")

**Checks**

* Independent double programming of every key output
* N in column headers = analysis set size
* Footnotes state population, method, and data cut
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Reproducibility**

* Version control (git) for programs and specifications
* Locked package versions (`renv.lock`)
* One command reruns everything (`lab/run_all.R`)

**Statistician's review**

* Does each number answer the SAP question?
* Are the denominators right?
* Do numbers agree across tables (events in 14.2.1 vs ADTTE vs IA report)?
:::
::::

# Part 5 · Interim analysis {background-color="#1D4F91" .part-title}

Boundaries, p-values, conditional power, the DMC report (12 minutes)

::: notes
Target: finish Part 5 by minute 82. Ask the room for a recommendation before showing the final result.
:::

## Running an interim analysis

```{=html}
<div class="flow">
  <div class="box review"><b>Track events</b>blinded, pooled across arms</div><div class="arrow">&rarr;</div>
  <div class="box review"><b>Set the DCO</b>date of the 61st event</div><div class="arrow">&rarr;</div>
  <div class="box review"><b>Clean data</b>up to the DCO</div><div class="arrow">&rarr;</div>
  <div class="box lead"><b>Re-run</b>the SAME ADaM and TFL programs with the cut</div><div class="arrow">&rarr;</div>
  <div class="box lead"><b>Independent statistician</b>unblinded closed report</div><div class="arrow">&rarr;</div>
  <div class="box lead"><b>DMC</b>closed session, recommendation</div><div class="arrow">&rarr;</div>
  <div class="box review"><b>Sponsor</b>hears only: continue / modify / stop</div>
</div>
```
* The sponsor's study team stays **blinded**: the unblinded work happens behind a firewall
* Open session (pooled data, conduct) vs closed session (by-arm efficacy and safety)

## The data cut in code: one program, many cuts

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r adam-datacut, opts.label = "code"}
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r adtte-interim, opts.label = "code"}
```

DCO = **`r format(ia_dco)`**, `r ia$events` events in High Dose + Placebo.
:::
::::

## Interim result against the boundary

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 8.5
#| fig-height: 5.2
p_ia_boundary
```
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
* Information fraction `r ia$events` / `r target_events` = `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * info_frac)`: Lan-DeMets spending evaluates the boundary **at the actual fraction**
* HR `r sprintf("%.2f (95%% CI %.2f, %.2f)", ia$hr, ia$hr_lower, ia$hr_upper)`
* Z = `r sprintf("%.3f", ia$z)`, one-sided p = `r fmt_p(ia$p_one_sided)`
* Efficacy needs Z ≥ `r sprintf("%.3f", z_eff_ia)` (p ≤ `r sprintf("%.4f", p_eff_ia)`): **not crossed**
* Futility guideline Z < 0: **not met**
:::
::::

## Conditional power {.code-small}

$$
\mathrm{CP}(\theta) = 1 - \Phi\!\left(\frac{c_K \sqrt{I_K} - Z_k \sqrt{I_k} - \theta\,(I_K - I_k)}{\sqrt{I_K - I_k}}\right),
\qquad I \approx \frac{\text{events}}{4},\quad \theta = -\log \mathrm{HR}
$$

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r ia-conditional-power, opts.label = "code"}
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
cp_tbl |>
  dplyr::mutate(theta = round(theta, 3), `Conditional power` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * `Conditional power`)) |>
  tab(20)
```

{rpact} `getAnalysisResults()` gives `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * cp_rpact_design)` under the design HR: same answer.

::: {.takeaway}
CP depends on the effect you assume. Under the design HR it is the most
optimistic number in the report; always show the current trend too.
:::
:::
::::

## Table IA.1 The DMC closed report (primary endpoint)

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
slide_gt(t_ia_1, 18)
```
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
**What would you recommend?**

* Pre-specified rule (Z < 0) says continue
* CP under the current trend is `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * cp_tbl[["Conditional power"]][2])`
* The final analysis gave HR `r sprintf("%.2f", pfs_hi$hr)`, p = `r fmt_p(pfs_hi$p_one_sided)`: the trial did not succeed

A futility rule on conditional power (for example CP < 10% under the current
trend) would have stopped earlier. Choosing the rule is a design decision,
made with its operating characteristics in mind.
:::
::::

## What else goes into the DMC report

:::: {.columns .small}
::: {.column width="50%"}
* Enrollment, disposition, protocol deviations, by arm
* Exposure and dose modifications
* AEs, serious AEs, deaths, labs: **safety is reviewed at every meeting**, efficacy only at planned interims
* Efficacy: Table IA.1, Kaplan-Meier by arm (Figure IA.1), conditional power
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 5
p_km_ia
```
:::


::: {.column width="48%"}
* **XPT**: SAS transport files, version 5 (names ≤ 8 characters, labels ≤ 40)
* **define.xml**: metadata for every dataset, variable, code list and derivation
* **aCRF**: annotated CRF
* **cSDRG / ADRG**: reviewer's guides for SDTM / ADaM
* Programs for the primary and key secondary results
* Conformance checks (Pinnacle 21) with explanations

[eCTD: electronic Common Technical Document; module 5 holds clinical study reports and data.]{.small .muted}

## Metadata-driven XPT files with {xportr}

:::: {.columns}

```{r sub-xportr, opts.label = "code"}
```
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r}
xpt_check |>
  head(12) |>
  tab(18)
```
:::
::::

## R in regulatory submissions

* FDA does not require any specific software (Statistical Software Clarifying Statement, 2015); it requires that you document and can reproduce what you did
* R Consortium submission pilots sent FDA R-based TFLs, a Shiny app and ADaM datasets built in R (github.com/RConsortium/submissions-wg)
* What reviewers need from an R submission:
  * package versions (`renv.lock`, `sessionInfo()`) and how to install them
  * programs that run on the submitted datasets and reproduce the CSR numbers
  * a reviewer's guide (ADRG) that explains all of this
* Many companies now run R and SAS side by side; double programming across languages is common

## Five things to take home {.larger}

1. **Write the SAP like code.** Every rule must be unambiguous; QC finds the gaps (`RFENDTC`).
2. **Power comes from events.** Design, forecast and monitor events, not patients.
3. **Traceability.** CRF field → raw → SDTM → ADaM → the number in the table.
4. **Interims reuse the final programs on a data cut**, and boundaries follow the actual information.
5. **Conditional power depends on the assumed effect.** Report it under the design and the current trend.

4. Open any script in `lab/R/`

**With Claude**

Open the repository with Claude (Claude Code, or a claude.ai project with the GitHub

* Add a sensitivity analysis: censor PFS after two missed scans
* Use the independent-review (BICR) assessments for PFS
